subject: Urgent: forensic logs & custody request for May 11 trading spike
messages:
From: Sara King <sara.king@macrofin.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
Cc: MacroFin Security <security@macrofin.com>
Date: Tue, 11 May 2027 14:22:00 -0400
Subject: Spike in latency and 5xx rates during 13:00-13:07 ET window — request for logs and custody procedure

Olga,

We observed a sharp latency increase and a rise in 5xx error rates between 13:00 and 13:07 ET today that impacted our pricing engine integrations. Our compliance team is requesting: a) request-level logs for the window (timestamps, request IDs, model version, route), b) confirmation of whether full prompt text was captured in any runtime store, and c) a chain-of-custody and hash manifest suitable for our auditors.

We need this as soon as possible; auditors may request evidence in their control review later this week. We also need to understand retention policies and whether any redaction was applied to the payloads you provide. If you can provide a small sample bundle and manifest with cryptographic hashes and an explanation of the preservation process, that will help us.

Please loop in whoever is needed from your ops/security teams.

Sara King
Head of Platform Reliability
MacroFin Bank

Attachment: incident-screenshots-11may.png (images referenced)
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
To: Sara King <sara.king@macrofin.com>
Cc: MacroFin Security <security@macrofin.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 11 May 2027 14:35:12 -0400
Subject: Re: Spike in latency and 5xx rates during 13:00-13:07 ET window — request for logs and custody procedure

Sara — thanks for the heads up and sorry for the disruption. I'm escalating to our on-call SRE and security leads now. Marcus and Evelyn, please see customer ask below and advise on forensic artifact availability and the custody steps we should follow.

Sara, quick clarifying Qs so we can scope the bundle:
- Confirm the precise time range you want (you mentioned 13:00–13:07 ET; do you want a 5-minute padding before/after?)
- Do you need raw request bodies, or are metadata + tokenized hashes sufficient for audit?
- Any legal hold/transfer instructions we should be aware of (DocuSign, PO reference)?

I'll coordinate delivery and provide a temporary S3 location + manifest once Marcus confirms.

—Olga
Olga Petrov
Account Executive, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>, Sara King <sara.king@macrofin.com>
Cc: MacroFin Security <security@macrofin.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 11 May 2027 15:02:06 -0400
Subject: Provisioning forensic bundle / what we can deliver now

Sara / Olga — I've pulled a preliminary forensic bundle for the 12:55–13:12 ET window (7 minutes padded each side) and staged artifacts for transfer. What I'm attaching/querying here:

Attachment manifest (staged):
- redwood-runtime-ops-20270511-manifest.txt — manifest with file list, sizes, SHA256 hashes
- partial-logs-stdout-20270511.gz — trimmed runtime request logs (request_id, timestamp, model_id, route, response_code, latency_ms). We have redacted end-user personal data fields per our PII redaction policy; raw prompt text removed unless explicitly configured by the customer.
- kvcache-checksum.txt — KV cache snapshot checksum for correlation
- evidence-request-form.pdf — our internal transfer form you can countersign for custody tracking

Notes and constraints:
- Our default hosted retention for full request bodies is 14 days; metadata and telemetry retention is 90 days. Dedicated/Private deployments can have custom retention, but your account is hosted.
- By default, we do NOT persist full raw prompt text in long-term object stores. Short-lived buffers may contain it during inference (<120s) but are rotated and not written to the object store except when customer opt-in is enabled.
- The logs we can provide now include full request_id and token-count info. For raw prompt text, we need explicit authorization or proof of legal hold.

Next steps I propose:
1) If MacroFin confirms it needs raw bodies for audit, we will provide a DocuSign-enabled evidence transfer and create a redaction plan (replace PII with stable tokens).
2) We will publish the manifest with SHA256 hashes and a procedural note describing how the archive was created (SRE on-call, time, host ids).

I'll generate the S3 pre-signed URL and post it to our secure drive once the transfer form is countersigned.

– Marcus Lin
Senior Site Reliability Engineer
Redwood Inference
From: MacroFin Security <security@macrofin.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 11 May 2027 16:07:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Provisioning forensic bundle / what we can deliver now

Marcus / Olga — thanks for the quick response. A few follow-ups from our auditors:
1) We require the manifest to include the specific hashing algorithm and the exact command used to create the archive to satisfy evidence reproducibility.
2) Please confirm whether any request payloads in the archive contain unredacted customer prompts. If any do, provide a list of request_ids that contain raw bodies.
3) Provide an exported access log for the S3 staging location including who requested/created the bundle and timestamps for each action.

If Redwood cannot produce raw prompt text, please state that explicitly; auditors will accept tokenized hashes if accompanied by your redaction policy and proof that the raw text was not written to persistent storage.

Sara King
MacroFin Bank — Security Audit Team
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
To: MacroFin Security <security@macrofin.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Sara King <sara.king@macrofin.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 11 May 2027 18:03:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Provisioning forensic bundle / what we can deliver now

Thanks — short answers and actions: 

1) Hashing & reproducibility: manifest will include SHA256 hashes and the exact tar + sha256sum commands we used. We will also provide the signing principal (on-call SRE) and timestamp (UTC).

2) Raw prompt text: Confirmed — Redwood hosted products do NOT persist raw prompt text to long-term object storage by default. The bundle we staged contains metadata and tokenized hashes only. There are no raw customer prompts in the staged partial-logs-stdout-20270511.gz. If MacroFin requires raw bodies, we need documented authorization or a signed legal hold; we will then extract, redact per policy, and produce a separate evidence archive (this is a manual flow).

3) S3 access log / custody trail: we will produce an exported access log for the staging bucket and include an evidence-transfer spreadsheet (who created, who downloaded, timestamps). The staged files have the following manifest hashes (sample):
- redwood-runtime-ops-20270511-manifest.txt : SHA256: 3f7a8b0c9f2e6a1b4a7d8e1c6b5e2f1d9a4c8e6b2f0d1c3a6b7e8f9d0c1a2b3c
- partial-logs-stdout-20270511.gz       : SHA256: 9b8c7d6e5f4a3b2c1d0e9f8a7b6c5d4e3f2a1b0c9d8e7f6a5b4c3d2e1f0a9b8c

Next steps: Marcus will upload the manifest + S3 access export to the secure Drive link (shared above) and I will trigger the evidence-request-form.pdf for MacroFin to countersign if raw bodies are required. We can also set a 48-hour preservation hold on the staged artifacts upon receipt of a signed form.

Olga Petrov
Account Executive, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
